title: Large Language Models Empowered Agent-based Modeling and Simulation: A Survey and Perspectives
publisher: arXiv (Tsinghua University; Gao, Lan, Li, Yuan, Ding, Zhou, Xu, Li)

key_points.claim: Survey frames LLM-driven ABMS as a new paradigm; organizes work into cyber, physical, social, and hybrid domains, and analyzes challenges in environment perception, human alignment, action generation, evaluation.
key_points.evidence_quote: systematically analyze the challenges in environment perception, human alignment, action generation, and evaluation.

key_points.claim: Classical ABM components are agents, environment and interaction. Agent capabilities needed are autonomy, social ability, reactivity and pro-activeness. Bounded rationality matters for economic and organizational realism.
key_points.evidence_quote: agents cannot make perfectly rational choices due to limitations of knowledge and computational capacity

key_points.claim: Traditional ABM methods are predefined rules (cellular automata), symbolic equations (social force model), stochastic models and ML/RL. Their limitations are simple reactive architectures, no general cross-environment agent, and no integrative descriptive/explanatory/predictive capability.
key_points.evidence_quote: existing methods cannot support the above tasks simultaneously: rule-based methods are useful in descriptive problems, while symbolic or stochastic methods can provide explanations

key_points.claim: Agent heterogeneity: traditional ABM struggles with parameter calibration and oversimplification. LLM agents can be customized through prompting, in-context learning or fine-tuning, and can play different roles in society.
key_points.evidence_quote: specialized and customized characteristics with prompting, in-context learning, or fine-tuning.

key_points.claim: Environments are virtual (sandboxes like Smallville, virtual software companies, recommender systems) or real (economies, real websites, urban digital twins). Interfaces are mostly text, and agent communication is text-based (direct) or rule-mediated (indirect).
key_points.evidence_quote: Most existing works use texts as the major interface, naturally due to the ability to understand and generate texts of large language models.

key_points.claim: Agent cognition architecture centers on planning (task decomposition, e.g. GITM, Voyager, AdaPlanner), memory (external memory store, Generative Agents) and reflection (Reflexion).
key_points.evidence_quote: planning dictates the course of action, memory provides a knowledge base derived from past experiences, and reflection adjusts strategies based on feedback.

key_points.claim: Alignment and personalization are done via prompt engineering or tuning. AI Town personas come from prompts. Prompted preferences (altruistic, selfish) change cooperation in games. Generated feedback aligned models 45x cheaper than crowd workers.
key_points.evidence_quote: the generated feedback enables LLM to achieve high human alignment 45× cheaper than hiring crowd workers

key_points.claim: Evaluation protocols are micro-level (individual behavior prediction) and macro-level (emergent regularities such as Okun's law), plus explanation elicitation and ethics/bias checks.
key_points.evidence_quote: macro-level evaluation is of great significance, which aims to evaluate whether the simulated process has the same pattern, regularity, etc., as the real-world data.

key_points.claim: Social networks and opinion dynamics: S3 replicates emotion, attitude and interaction behavior on real network data. LLM agents reproduce multi-peak epidemic curves, exhibit conformity and wisdom-of-crowds, and echo human content biases.
key_points.evidence_quote: LLM exhibits preferences for stereotype-consistent, negative, socially oriented, and threat-related content

key_points.claim: Cooperation and organization: role-playing multi-agent frameworks simulate teams and institutions (ChatDev, MetaGPT, CAMEL, AgentVerse, MAD debate, COLA stance detection). Early ones lacked versatility, and AgentVerse generates agents adaptively.
key_points.evidence_quote: CHATDEV [163] is a virtual software development company where LLM Agents collaborate to develop computer software, with different roles for agents including CEO, CTO, designers, and programmers.

key_points.claim: Individual social behavior: LLM agents can act as survey/human-subject proxies. Humanoid Agents add needs, emotions and relational closeness.
key_points.evidence_quote: synthetic responses generated by large language models cannot be easily distinguished from human data

key_points.claim: Economics: LLMs replicate behavioral-economics phenomena (Horton), show largely rational budget choices, and beat most students on TUCE. Forecasting is mixed (worse than SOTA on stocks, comparable to SPF for inflation).
key_points.evidence_quote: GPT performs largely rationally in risk, time, social, and food preferences domains in terms of budgetary decisions.

key_points.claim: Game-theory and market simulations: prompted personalities alter cooperation, and LLMs fall short of Nash equilibrium and coordinate poorly (GPT-4 defects after one defection). Restaurant-competition sims show price convergence and a Matthew effect. Duopoly agents collude when they can communicate.
key_points.evidence_quote: in the absence of communication, prices tend to approach the Bertrand equilibrium price. However, with communication, collusion between the companies tends to bring prices closer to the monopoly price.

key_points.claim: Hybrid macroeconomic simulation (Li et al.) scales to hundreds of LLM agents and reproduces the Phillips curve and Okun's law, which rule-based ABM and RL baselines did not.
key_points.evidence_quote: only the simulation based on LLM agents can produce the correct Phillips curve

key_points.claim: Hybrid/urban/historical sims: Generative Agents (memory, reflection, planning) produced emergent events like Valentine's Day parties and mayoral elections. WarAgent simulates WWI, WWII and Warring States. UGI is an urban digital-twin platform.
key_points.evidence_quote: this approach led to complex social scenarios, such as Valentine’s Day parties and mayoral elections

key_points.claim: Physical and cyber domains: LLM agents simulate navigation, driving (CARLA driver agent reduces collisions), wireless-network users, web browsing (WebAgent, Mind2Web, WebArena) and recommender-system users (RecAgent, Agent4Rec reproduce filter bubbles).
key_points.evidence_quote: The proposed agents can emulate the filter bubble effect and discover the underlying causal relationships in recommendation tasks.

key_points.claim: Open problems: scaling large societies is computationally expensive (batch prompting gives up to 5x efficiency), benchmarks for simulation fidelity are lacking, open platforms for LLM-driven ABS are lacking, and robustness and adversarial propagation remain open.
key_points.evidence_quote: the assessment of LLM-driven agent simulation is still inadequate.

key_points.claim: Ethical risks: persona assignment raises toxicity about 6x, and simulated demographic groups are caricatured. Biases can be amplified in multi-agent transmission chains.
key_points.evidence_quote: when certain personas are assigned to ChatGPT it will generate output with 6× toxicity

reliability_notes: Full text of the arXiv preprint (v1, Dec 2023). It is a survey, so findings are secondhand summaries of the cited studies. Some cited works were unreviewed preprints or ICLR submissions under review. The survey predates 2024 developments. Its taxonomy is useful for organizing by aspect (agents, environment, interaction, cognition, evaluation, domains).
